title: Uniform finite-coefficient etale open-image Tor bound
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^n1_A=0$ for some $n\ge1$, including the zero ring. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open $k$-immersion between separated schemes of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. On the small etale sites use constant-$A$ module sheaves, their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], total right derived module direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then $d_j=\operatorname{cd}(j)$, the torsion etale cohomological dimension [def-kun-cd], is a finite nonnegative integer depending only on $j$. For every $A$-module sheaf $F$ and $q>d_j$, $R^qj_*F=0$. For every $a\le b$ and $L\in D^b_c(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ against all degree-zero module sheaves [def-kun-tor-amplitude], put $Q=Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}L$. For every finite $A$-module $M$, the canonical projection map [def-kun-projection-formula-map]
$$Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_X\longrightarrow Rj_{\mathrm{et},*}(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_U)$$
is an isomorphism, where $M_T$ is the constant module sheaf [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. The object $Q$ is bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+d_j]$ against every degree-zero etale $A_X$-module sheaf. No separable-closedness or absolute cohomological-dimension hypothesis on $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite A open-image case; returned proof steps 3--5. Relative bound: Stacks Tag 0F10, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-finite-cd (1); definition-cd-f. Finite-constant projection and arbitrary-field all-module Tor argument are the auxiliary arguments isolated here.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-kun-0f10] to the $k$-morphism $j:U\to X$: both schemes are of finite type over the same field. Thus $\operatorname{cd}(j)<\infty$. By [def-kun-cd] this dimension is the least nonnegative integer bounding the higher direct images of all torsion abelian sheaves. Set $d_j=\operatorname{cd}(j)$. This choice depends only on $j$, and clause (1) imposes no separable-closedness or absolute cohomological-dimension hypothesis on $k$.

Let F be any A-module sheaf. Since A is finite, its additive group is torsion, and every A-module is additively torsion (IsAddTorsion.module_of_finite). The sectionwise torsion criterion makes the forgotten abelian sheaf torsion, including when A is the zero ring. Apply the defining bound of cd(j) from step 1. The comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies the forgotten module higher image with this abelian higher image; faithfulness of forgetting reflects its zero identity. Finally the canonical bounded-below/unbounded right-derived compatibility identifies this vanishing with H^q(Rj_*(F[0])) for every integer q>d.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree; Tag 072W, higher direct images as sheafified cohomology; relative bound from etale-cohomology.tex definition-cd-f

proof.text: The finite ring A is Noetherian, and every finite A-module is finitely presented, by the existing finite-module and Noetherian finite-presentation results. Bounded constructibility of L gives its upper cohomology bound. Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] with f=j and N=d, using step 2 in natural degrees. The resulting finiteConstantProjectionMap is the canonical projection component followed by the canonical constant-pullback identifications and functor associators. Unfold only this natural-transformation composite and cancel its invertible second factor; the original projection component is therefore invertible.

source.place: Statement and proof: Noetherian finite-syzygy approximation and the uniform cohomological-dimension bound

proof.text: Put $Q=Rj_*L$. The complex $L$ belongs to $D^+$ because it is bounded. The hypotheses of [lem-sf-open-tor-bound-finite-constant-tests] hold with $V=U$, $T=X$ and $e=d_j$: step 2 supplies the bound on every module sheaf, step 3 supplies every finite-constant projection isomorphism, and the input Tor interval is $[a,b]$. Consequently $\mathcal H^q(Q\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_X)=0$ for every finite $A$-module $M$ and every $q<a$ or $q>b+d_j$. In particular the upper shift here is the relative $d_j$, not a bound on the absolute cohomology of $k$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite A open-image clause, expanded by the existing finite-constant-tests lemma; its derived bounds follow derived.tex Tag 07K7 (4)(c)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-open-tor-bound-stalk-filtered-extension] on $X$ to $Q$ and the endpoints $a,b+d_j$, using the finite-constant vanishings from step 4. Its conclusion is Tor amplitude $[a,b+d_j]$ against every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf, as required. This uses the finite-ring stalk/filtered-union test, which has no ground-field hypothesis and requires no constructibility of the test sheaves. Thus the constant tests have been extended to the full all-module-sheaf definition.

source.place: Paragraph (3), finite A open-image clause, all-module Tor conclusion; existing stalk-filtered-extension lemma, using sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0DEN and exact filtered colimits

proof.text: Finally $\ell^n$ is invertible in $k$, since $\ell\ne p$. The ring $A$ is finite and killed by this invertible integer, and $j$ is an open immersion of finite-type schemes over the field $k$. Hence [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients], applied to $L\in D^b_c(U,A)$, gives $Q\in D^b_c(X,A)$. Together with steps 1--5 this proves all clauses. The zero ring has only zero unital module sheaves, so the same conclusions include it; the cohomological dimension $d_j$ is still the coefficient-independent torsion dimension of $j$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q117-8348ff198 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Shape: one commit, the item JSON and the report. There are no new nodes and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Six steps cite seven existing nodes, and I checked every hypothesis of each. (1) lem-kun-0f10 clause (1), read against Stacks 0F10 lemma-finite-cd(1): cd(f)<inf for finite-type schemes over any field, so d_j=cd(j) is finite and depends only on j (def-kun-cd). (2) lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison holds for any ring including 0: the underlying sheaf is l^n-torsion, so module R^q j_*F vanishes for q>d_j. (3) lem-sf-projection-finite-constant: a finite ring is Noetherian, a finite module is finitely presented, L is in D^-, N=d_j, and its map is the item's adjunction-mate projection map; no perfectness is needed (checked M=A/eps over F_l[eps]/eps^2). (4) lem-sf-open-tor-bound-finite-constant-tests: same k, l, A and qc open immersion, L in D^+, e=d_j; it gives finite-constant vanishing outside [a,b+d_j]. (5) lem-sf-open-tor-bound-stalk-filtered-extension: finite commutative A, any scheme, gives the all-module Tor amplitude. (6) cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients: any field, l^n invertible, gives D^b_c. Edge cases A=0, U empty, j=id, a=b and cd(k)=inf all hold. The closure of the cited nodes contains neither the item nor its parent lem-sfb-finite-open-direct-image-ctf, so there is no cycle. Blueprint main-20261015 direct-images paragraph (3) and det-cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-open-tor assume a separably closed field, so they cannot be substituted for this arbitrary-field item. The six tool_uses are accepted as black boxes. Advisory: existing node lem-sf-open-tor-bound-arbitrary-field (Q93) already states steps 4-5 combined, and those steps could cite it directly; this is a correct alternative, not a fault. No changes.
